title: FOUR KILOMETRES OF THIN ICE
deck: Twenty-three people breathe the last of their air under four kilometres of ice, and a rescue vessel built to survive exactly one trip.
shape: Rescue under a clock in six scenes: the hull's one excursion is spent on a tool instead of on seats, the tide sets the windows, and the people who wait are given the last word on when they cross.

scenes.title: The Placard
paragraphs: *Marrow Station, surface of the moon Tavret · Hour 0*
The air clock for Halcyon was a magnetic placard on the control-room wall, and someone had been changing its digits by hand. It read 31:00. Underneath, in marker, a second number: 23.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
Halcyon sits on the sea floor, four thousand and ten metres below this floor: three thousand three hundred and fifty of ice, then six hundred and sixty of water. Twenty-three people, thirty-one hours of air at the rate they breathe now, saturated at six bar, so they cannot simply be pulled up. The shaft froze round the lift cage at 03:40. We have one vessel that can go down: Curlew, a drone-sub, six seats, nine hours from launch to Halcyon's door.
Illuminara stood at the placard rather than the screens. Nobody had yet asked her to sit.

**Imre Solano**  
The hull is certified for one excursion below three thousand metres. Down and back, to anywhere past that line. Two of twelve test hulls cracked on the second. I won't fly a second one, and you shouldn't ask me to.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
So six come up. Seventeen don't. I have been told to draw lots, and I would rather resign.

**Illuminara**  
What exactly does the certificate count?

**Imre Solano**  
Pressure excursions. Full cycles past the line.

**Illuminara**  
Then the excursion is the scarce thing, not the seats. I'd like to ask what it is best spent on before we ask who sits in it.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
It carries six. That's what it is for.

**Illuminara**  
Who says the cage is dead?

**Ofelia Brandt**  
It stopped moving, and the shaft is ice around it.

**Illuminara**  
Stopped is not dead. May I see what it has been saying since 03:40?

scenes.title: The Trace
paragraphs: *Halcyon, 4,010 m below · Hour 2*
The habitat's voice came up the cable thin and a little late. Illuminara spoke to the commander first and the engineer second.

**Marit Osei**  
I've heard about the lots. I will not run them. If someone has a plan that is not a plan to choose who dies, say it quickly, because my people are watching me listen.

**Illuminara**  
I have a question rather than a plan. Maud Okonkwo logged the cage's frame strain. Maud, there is a wobble in it.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
Sensor noise. It rises and falls, a third or so. I flagged it and wrote it off.

Illuminara laid the trace beside a second line: the swell and slackening of the ice shell as Tavret's orbit pulled it. The peaks of the wobble sat on the peaks of the flex, every three hours and fourteen minutes.

**Illuminara**  
Noise does not keep the moon's time. I think the cage is held by ice that is squeezed against it, and every time the shell relaxes, the squeeze eases. That gives us a door that opens for a few minutes every three hours and fourteen.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
Then you have the wrong picture, and it matters. The shaft is clear above and below. The cage climbs on pinions, on a rack; the cable is only voice and power. The ice is on three roller carriages and fourteen metres of rack at the collar, glazed over the teeth. Free those and the cage is free.

*Fourteen metres, not a plug a hundred long.* Illuminara took the correction the way she took a good measurement, with gratitude and without ceremony. It made the plan smaller. It also made it possible.

**Marit Osei**  
And you want my people to bet their lives on a wobble.

**Illuminara**  
I want them to measure it, which costs only waiting. The next peak is at Hour 6 and twenty-six minutes. If the strain does not fall by at least a third and stay down for five minutes, I am wrong, and the director's lots are the plan. I'll say so myself.

scenes.title: One Excursion
paragraphs: *Marrow Station, control room · Hour 6, 26 minutes*
Maud Okonkwo read the number up the cable as it fell, and the room, which had not been quiet, became so.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
Down thirty-eight percent. Holding. Five minutes. Nine. It's coming back up now.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
So the door exists. What holds it?

**Illuminara**  
I do, partly, and I want you to hear my limit rather than guess it. At a peak I can carry the cage's whole weight for eight minutes. At a trough, ninety seconds. On glazed rack the pinions skip and the carriages carry nothing, so for those fourteen metres someone must lift all of it. I can lift that, or I can keep the ice walls from closing on a cut lane. Not both for more than ninety seconds.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
Seats save six and spend the hull.

**Illuminara**  
And leave seventeen with air and nothing left to come for them. A second excursion is the other road, and Imre has told us what it costs.

**Imre Solano**  
Then the walls need something else.

**Illuminara**  
A frame. Four titanium struts to jack the lane open to a metre, and a hot-water lance for the carriages. The struts hold the walls and I hold the weight, and neither of us holds the other's share. Curlew carries it in the seat bay; Imre began swapping seats for struts at Hour 3, under protest, as a job that can be undone. It goes down once, to the collar, and comes home. It never touches a passenger.

**Imre Solano**  
Each strut seats in a socket drilled into the collar casting, is good for a hundred and forty kilonewtons, and is rated for forty troughs. At a trough the ice leans on each with about eighty. The frame runs on its own cells for sixty hours and reads up the cable's data pair, so it does not need Curlew once it is placed. The cancel line is a hundred and twenty kilonewtons on any strut, or three centimetres of total walk in any socket, counted from installation. Past it the frame is finished and so is every crossing after. I read them at every trough, and nobody boards until I have read one with the cage gone.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
And if your eight minutes fail?

**Illuminara**  
Then Curlew is spent and so are we, and I will have cost you the six. I am sure of the arithmetic, not of the ice. So the first window frees an empty cage. If I fail there, nobody is in it.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
The cage runs two-tenths of a metre a second. Fifty-five minutes between the collar and us, four hours thirty-nine between the collar and the surface. Windows from 9:40, every three-fourteen. Which can we afford to miss?

**Illuminara**  
The frame at 9:40, the cage free by 9:48 and with you at 10:43. If twelve are aboard by 11:55 it meets the collar at 12:50 and crosses at the 12:54 window, and they dock at the surface at 17:40. Empty, it is back at the collar at 22:40, four minutes after the 22:36 window. So it crosses at 25:50, reaches you at 26:52, and the eleven cross at 29:04 and dock at 33:50.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
Air is the other clock, and it's mine. Thirty-one hours at twenty-three people. The twelve you take first are the stretcher cases and the over-fifties, and they are fifty-nine percent of what Halcyon breathes. When they go at 11:55 there are nineteen hours and five minutes left at the old rate. The eleven stretch that to forty-six and a half. Halcyon is dead at 58:27.

**Illuminara**  
The cage carries eight hours of its own air and needs under six from the landing to the surface, so the eleven can seal themselves into it as late as an hour before Halcyon dies. The last window that works is 58:10. Anything before it, we can afford to miss.

**Imre Solano**  
Three hours to the collar, and ten minutes to deploy. The other six hours of the nine are open water and a blind dock, and we are not going there. I leave at 6:30, and I fly it once.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
Then fly.

scenes.title: The Order
paragraphs: *Halcyon, crew deck and wet porch · Hour 7*
The cage was rated for twelve, by weight on the rack. That left a number nobody wanted to say, and Commander Osei said it.

**Marit Osei**  
Twelve now. Eleven later. Which of you goes first is our decision, not the surface's, and it is not going to be a draw.

**Anselm Dube**  
I'll propose, and you can tear it up. First lift: the stretcher cases, the over-fifties, the three who feel the cold worst. Everyone whose body gets less safe the longer it waits. They also breathe fastest, so when they go, the rest have forty-six hours.

**Kofi Mensah**  
And who is last?

**Anselm Dube**  
The ones who can still work. Maud, those of us who know the rack, the commander.

**Kofi Mensah**  
That isn't an order, that's a sentence. You're making the strongest wait because they can.

**Marit Osei**  
Yes. So here is what goes with the sentence. The last eleven choose the hour. Imre's line is the line: past a hundred and twenty kilonewtons or three centimetres of walk, nobody crosses and nobody argues. Inside it, any one of us can refuse a crossing, and nobody is carried against a refusal. The surface does not get a vote.

**Anselm Dube**  
One voice can cost all eleven of us a window.

**Marit Osei**  
A window costs three hours fourteen of our own air, which we can count. A crossing costs what it costs, which we can't.
Then she asked the harder thing as a question. The cage would land on six metres of iced rack, and someone had to go out through the porch and clear it with a hot hose before 10:40.

**Marit Osei**  
Nobody is ordered. If nobody goes, we clear it from inside the cage, which costs eighteen minutes of boarding. The first lift misses 12:54 and waits for 16:08. I am telling you the price so that you can say no knowing it.

**Anselm Dube**  
Everyone in this room owes the table three days of decompression. A body that has worked the porch owes forty hours more. Nobody should pretend that is nothing.

Two people said no, plainly, and Marit marked their names down without a word. Maud Okonkwo went because she alone knew the rack, Anselm because he had worked a porch before, and Kofi Mensah because he had asked what the strong owed the sick and had not liked the silence that followed. Maud was back through the lock by 9:25 with ice in her cuffs, and took the headset.

scenes.title: Eight Minutes
paragraphs: *The collar, 3,350 m down · Hour 9, 40 minutes*

Illuminara had come down beside the cable, past the point where light was an idea, and the cold and the pressure meant what they always meant to her, which was information. She could read where it carried load, and where it was about to close.
Curlew hung at the collar with the frame folded in its belly. Solano's voice in the water was calm and slightly hoarse.

**Imre Solano**  
Struts deploying. Lane walls at one metre. Lance in two minutes. Peak window opens now.

The struts took the walls. That was the arrangement, and it was a relief to be only the other half of it. She took the cage's weight. It came into her like a held note, fourteen tonnes of rack and steel that the ice was trying to keep. The first carriage let go at minute two. The second at minute four. The third did not.

**Imre Solano**  
Carriage three isn't releasing. Minute five. Three left.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
That carriage has a shear pin on the east face. It's the one I always said we should replace. Hit it from the east.

Solano swung the lance. Illuminara felt the pin go, a small bright failure, and the cage dropped out of the ice onto clean rack and its own pinions for the first time since 03:40. She released it at minute seven and fifty seconds.

**Illuminara**  
That is as long as I can hold. If it had needed ten seconds more, it would not have been me who could give them.

The cage ran down toward the habitat, empty, at a stately two-tenths of a metre a second, and the voices from Halcyon began to cheer, and she let them. She did not go up. The windows would not wait for her to come back down, so she stayed in the lee of the frame, in the dark.
At 11:17, in the first trough, the struts took the ice alone, and Solano, rising in Curlew, read them off the telemetry: fifty-eight percent of rating, eleven millimetres of walk.

**Imre Solano**  
Inside. Board them.

They were aboard at 11:55, twelve of them, with the stretchers latched. At 12:50 the cage came up to the collar, and this time there was weight in it, and the weight had names. She held it across the fourteen metres for seven minutes and thirty seconds. The struts held the walls. Curlew broke the surface at 12:55, its excursion spent, flown once as promised.

The cage went on up the open bore, four hours and thirty-nine minutes of it, with six bar held inside. At 17:40 its door mated to the chamber door at Marrow Station and the first twelve began to come down to surface pressure at the pace their bodies allowed.

scenes.title: The Second Ride
paragraphs: *The collar, 3,350 m down · Hour 22, 40 minutes*

The empty cage came down the bore on schedule, and that was the trouble. It stopped at the glazed rack four minutes after the 22:36 peak, and Illuminara felt the squeeze already coming back through the ice.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
Four minutes. Say it plainly so we can stop doing sums. Can you hold it?

**Illuminara**  
Not across. I would have under three minutes and the crossing needs seven. The ice would close on the cage in the middle of the rack. The next window is 25:50.
Nobody on the cable suggested she try. Her being sure of a limit had never cost anyone anything before; now it cost three hours and fourteen minutes of air that Halcyon could count.

The frame stood alone through the long wait, on its own cells, reading up the cable's data pair, and Maud logged every trough. Walk of 1.4 centimetres at 14:31. Two point zero at 17:45. Two point six at 20:59, inside the line. Then, at 24:13, with the cage parked above it and nothing moving, two point two.
At 25:50 Illuminara carried the empty cage across. At 26:52 it settled on the landing the porch team had cleared, and eleven people mustered at the cage door at the pace of people who could walk.

**Imre Solano**  
Trough, 27:27. One hundred and four kilonewtons, walk two point six centimetres. The line is one-twenty and three. It is inside the line, and I would let you cross.

**Marit Osei**  
Inside the line, then it's ours. One voice is enough. Who refuses?

**Kofi Mensah**  
I do. One window. Look at the log: at 20:59 it read two point six, and at 24:13 it was back to two point two with nobody touching it. I would rather pay in air than cross on two point six with eleven people in the cage.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
He's reading the trace correctly. It does relax.

**Anselm Dube**  
Three hours fourteen.

**Marit Osei**  
Counted. We have twenty-nine hours of air and the crossing needs five. Refusal stands. We cross at 32:18.

They waited. At 30:41 the trough read two point three centimetres. At 31:15 the cage left the landing, and at 32:18 Illuminara took its weight, tired, and carried it across in seven minutes and fifteen seconds, fifteen seconds under what she had said. Then she rose beside it for four hours and thirty-nine minutes at two-tenths of a metre a second, a speed she found tedious and kept to.
At 37:04 the door mated. Marit Osei was the last one through it.

**Marit Osei**  
That's the eleven. You can tell your director the habitat is switched off.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
The company will want to know whose fault the freeze was.

**Marit Osei**  
The company can write it on whatever placard it likes. Twenty-three people are in a chamber with a door.

Maud, Anselm and Kofi would spend their extra forty hours on the table without complaint. Illuminara sat on the floor of the control room for the first time since she had come up. She did not pretend to be anything but tired. She said so, plainly, to the room, and to Solano.
On the wall, someone had finally wiped off the digits. In their place, in marker, was the number 23, and a line under it.

critic_line: Twenty-three people escape four kilometres of ice because Illuminara spends a one-use vessel on a tool rather than on six seats, states exactly where her own strength ends, and leaves the trapped crew the evidence and authority to choose the final crossing.

literary_score.method: Independent GPT 7D SA1 and Claude PEC-6 final scores; equal 50/50 model weight.
shared_strengths: Both judges found the rescue solution technically legible and governed by hard clocks, thresholds and load constraints rather than convenient revelation.
Both judges praised the distributed agency: specialists correct the plan, the trapped crew controls risk, and refusal changes the actual rescue schedule.
shared_reservations: Both judges noted that several secondary characters are defined more by operational roles than by private texture, while technical dialogue can read like a polished briefing.
Both judges found Illuminara's capacities and inner experience comparatively abstract, limiting emotional and sensory intimacy.

translation_sl.title: ŠTIRJE KILOMETRI TANKEGA LEDU
translation_sl.deck: Triindvajset ljudi diha zadnji zrak pod štirimi kilometri ledu, reševalno plovilo pa je zgrajeno tako, da prenese natanko eno pot.
translation_sl.shape: Reševanje pod časovnim pritiskom v šestih prizorih: trup svojo edino odpravo porabi za orodje namesto za sedeže, plimovanje določa časovna okna, ljudje, ki čakajo, pa dobijo zadnjo besedo o tem, kdaj bodo prečkali.

scenes.title: Tabla
paragraphs: *Postaja Marrow, površje lune Tavret · Ura 0*
Zračna ura za Halcyon je bila magnetna tabla na steni nadzorne sobe in nekdo je njene številke spreminjal na roko. Kazala je 31:00. Pod njo je bilo s flomastrom zapisano drugo število: 23.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
Halcyon leži na morskem dnu, štiri tisoč deset metrov pod temi tlemi: tri tisoč tristo petdeset metrov ledu, nato šeststo šestdeset metrov vode. Triindvajset ljudi, enaintrideset ur zraka pri sedanji hitrosti dihanja, nasičeni pri šestih barih, zato jih ne moremo preprosto potegniti navzgor. Jašek je ob 03:40 zamrznil okoli dvigalne kletke. Imamo eno plovilo, ki lahko gre dol: Curlew, brezpilotno podmornico s šestimi sedeži, devet ur od izplutja do vrat Halcyona.
Illuminara je stala pri tabli, ne pri zaslonih. Nihče je še ni prosil, naj sede.

**Imre Solano**  
Trup je certificiran za eno odpravo pod tri tisoč metrov. Dol in nazaj, kamor koli pod to mejo. Dva od dvanajstih preizkusnih trupov sta pri drugi odpravi počila. Drugega ne bom upravljal in tudi vi me ne bi smeli prositi.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
Torej jih šest pride gor. Sedemnajst jih ne. Naročili so mi, naj žrebam, jaz pa bi raje odstopila.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj natančno šteje certifikat?

**Imre Solano**  
Tlačne odprave. Celotne cikle prek meje.

**Illuminara**  
Potem je redka dobrina odprava, ne sedeži. Preden vprašamo, kdo naj sede vanj, bi rada vprašala, za kaj jo je najbolje porabiti.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
Prepelje jih šest. Temu je namenjeno.

**Illuminara**  
Kdo pravi, da je kletka mrtva?

**Ofelia Brandt**  
Nehala se je premikati in jašek okoli nje je zaledenel.

**Illuminara**  
Ustavljeno ni mrtvo. Smem videti, kaj sporoča od 03:40?

scenes.title: Sled
paragraphs: *Halcyon, 4.010 m spodaj · Ura 2*
Glas habitata je po kablu prihajal šibek in z rahlo zamudo. Illuminara je najprej govorila s poveljnico in nato z inženirko.

**Marit Osei**  
Slišala sem za žreb. Ne bom ga izvedla. Če ima kdo načrt, ki ni načrt izbire, kdo bo umrl, naj ga hitro pove, ker moji ljudje gledajo, kako poslušam.

**Illuminara**  
Namesto načrta imam vprašanje. Maud Okonkwo je beležila napetost ogrodja kletke. Maud, v zapisu je nihanje.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
Šum tipala. Dviga se in pada za približno tretjino. Označila sem ga in odpisala.

Illuminara je sled položila ob drugo črto: naraščanje in popuščanje ledenega ovoja, ko ga je vlekla Tavretova orbita. Vrhovi nihanja so se ujemali z vrhovi upogiba, vsakih tri ure in štirinajst minut.

**Illuminara**  
Šum se ne ravna po luninem času. Mislim, da kletko drži led, stisnjen obnjo, in vsakič, ko ovoj popusti, pritisk oslabi. Tako dobimo vrata, ki se vsakih tri ure in štirinajst minut za nekaj minut odprejo.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
Potem si predstavljaš narobe, in to je pomembno. Jašek je nad in pod kletko čist. Kletka se vzpenja z zobniki po zobati letvi; kabel prenaša samo glas in elektriko. Led je na treh vozičkih z valji in na štirinajstih metrih letve pri ovratniku, kjer so zobje poledeneli. Osvobodite to in kletka bo prosta.
*Štirinajst metrov, ne sto metrov dolg čep.* Illuminara je popravek sprejela tako, kot je sprejela dobro meritev, s hvaležnostjo in brez slovesnosti. Načrt je postal manjši. Postal je tudi mogoč.

**Marit Osei**  
In želiš, da moji ljudje zastavijo življenja na nihanju.

**Illuminara**  
Želim, da ga izmerijo, kar stane samo čakanje. Naslednji vrh bo ob uri 6 in šestindvajset minut. Če napetost ne pade za vsaj tretjino in ne ostane nizka pet minut, se motim in načrt direktorice je žreb. Sama bom to povedala.

scenes.title: Ena odprava
paragraphs: *Postaja Marrow, nadzorna soba · Ura 6, 26 minut*
Maud Okonkwo je po kablu odčitavala številko, ko je padala, in soba, ki prej ni bila tiha, je utihnila.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
Dol za osemintrideset odstotkov. Drži. Pet minut. Devet. Zdaj spet raste.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
Torej vrata obstajajo. Kaj jih drži odprta?

**Illuminara**  
Deloma jaz, in želim, da slišite mojo omejitev, namesto da o njej ugibate. Na vrhu lahko osem minut nosim vso težo kletke. Na dnu devetdeset sekund. Na poledeneli letvi zobniki preskakujejo in vozički ne nosijo ničesar, zato mora na teh štirinajstih metrih nekdo dvigniti vse. Lahko dvignem to ali pa preprečim, da bi se ledene stene zaprle nad izrezanim prehodom. Obojega ne morem početi dlje kot devetdeset sekund.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
Sedeži rešijo šest ljudi in porabijo trup.

**Illuminara**  
Sedemnajstim pa pustijo zrak, ne da bi ostalo kaj, kar bi lahko prišlo ponje. Druga odprava je druga možnost in Imre nam je povedal, koliko stane.

**Imre Solano**  
Potem mora stene držati nekaj drugega.

**Illuminara**  
Ogrodje. Štirje titanovi oporniki, ki bodo prehod razprli na en meter, in sulica z vročo vodo za vozičke. Oporniki držijo stene, jaz pa težo, in nobeden od naju ne nosi deleža drugega. Curlew to prepelje v prostoru za sedeže; Imre je ob uri 3 pod protestom začel zamenjevati sedeže z oporniki, kot delo, ki se še lahko razveljavi. Enkrat se spusti do ovratnika in se vrne domov. Nikoli se ga ne dotakne potnik.

**Imre Solano**  
Vsak opornik sede v ležišče, izvrtano v ulitek ovratnika, prenese sto štirideset kilonjutnov in je predviden za štirideset dolin. V dolini led pritiska na vsakega s približno osemdesetimi. Ogrodje šestdeset ur deluje na lastne celice in podatke bere po paru v kablu, zato Curlewa po namestitvi ne potrebuje. Meja za preklic je sto dvajset kilonjutnov na katerem koli oporniku ali skupni premik katerega koli ležišča za tri centimetre, merjeno od namestitve. Ko jo presežemo, je ogrodja konec in z njim vsakega naslednjega prečkanja. Odčitke preverim v vsaki dolini in nihče ne vstopi, dokler ne preberem enega po odhodu kletke.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
In če tvojih osem minut ne bo dovolj?

**Illuminara**  
Potem bo Curlew porabljen in z njim tudi mi, jaz pa vas bom stala tistih šestih. Prepričana sem o računu, ne o ledu. Zato prvo okno osvobodi prazno kletko. Če mi tam spodleti, v njej ne bo nikogar.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
Kletka se premika dve desetinki metra na sekundo. Petinpetdeset minut med ovratnikom in nami, štiri ure devetintrideset med ovratnikom in površjem. Okna se odprejo od 9:40 naprej, vsake tri štirinajst. Katera lahko zgrešimo?

**Illuminara**  
Ogrodje ob 9:40, kletka prosta do 9:48 in pri vas ob 10:43. Če je dvanajst ljudi vkrcanih do 11:55, doseže ovratnik ob 12:50 in ga prečka v oknu ob 12:54, na površju pa pristane ob 17:40. Prazna se vrne do ovratnika ob 22:40, štiri minute po oknu ob 22:36. Zato prečka ob 25:50, do vas prispe ob 26:52, enajsterica pa prečka ob 29:04 in pristane ob 33:50.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
Zrak je druga ura in zanjo sem odgovorna jaz. Enaintrideset ur za triindvajset ljudi. Dvanajsterica, ki jo odpeljete prva, so bolniki na nosilih in starejši od petdeset let, skupaj pa porabijo devetinpetdeset odstotkov vsega, kar diha Halcyon. Ko odidejo ob 11:55, pri stari porabi ostane devetnajst ur in pet minut. Enajsterica to raztegne na šestinštirideset ur in pol. Halcyon ugasne ob 58:27.

**Illuminara**  
Kletka ima osem ur lastnega zraka in od pristanka do površja potrebuje manj kot šest, zato se lahko enajsterica vanjo zapre še eno uro pred smrtjo Halcyona. Zadnje uporabno okno je ob 58:10. Vsako prej si lahko privoščimo zgrešiti.

**Imre Solano**  
Tri ure do ovratnika in deset minut za namestitev. Drugih šest ur od devetih odpade na odprto vodo in slepo pristajanje, tja pa ne gremo. Odhajam ob 6:30 in upravljam ga enkrat.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
Potem poleti.

scenes.title: Vrstni red
paragraphs: *Halcyon, paluba posadke in mokra preddverna komora · Ura 7*
Kletka je bila po nosilnosti zobate letve predvidena za dvanajst ljudi. Tako je ostalo število, ki ga nihče ni želel izreči, in poveljnica Osei ga je izrekla.

**Marit Osei**  
Dvanajst zdaj. Enajst pozneje. Kdo med vami gre prvi, je naša odločitev, ne odločitev površja, in ne bomo žrebali.

**Anselm Dube**  
Predlagal bom, vi pa lahko predlog zavržete. Prvo dvigalo: bolniki na nosilih, starejši od petdeset let, trije, ki najtežje prenašajo mraz. Vsi, katerih telo je manj varno, čim dlje čakajo. Tudi najhitreje dihajo, zato bo drugim po njihovem odhodu ostalo šestinštirideset ur.

**Kofi Mensah**  
In kdo gre zadnji?

**Anselm Dube**  
Tisti, ki še lahko delamo. Maud, tisti med nami, ki poznamo letev, poveljnica.

**Kofi Mensah**  
To ni vrstni red, to je obsodba. Najmočnejše silite čakati zato, ker zmorejo.

**Marit Osei**  
Da. Zato obsodbo spremlja naslednje. Zadnjih enajst izbere uro. Imrejeva meja je meja: čez sto dvajset kilonjutnov ali tri centimetre premika nihče ne prečka in nihče se ne prepira. Znotraj nje lahko kateri koli od nas zavrne prečkanje in nikogar ne bodo odnesli proti njegovi zavrnitvi. Površje nima glasovalne pravice.

**Anselm Dube**  
En glas lahko vseh enajst stane celo okno.

**Marit Osei**  
Okno stane tri ure in štirinajst minut našega lastnega zraka, ki jih lahko preštejemo. Prečkanje stane, kolikor pač stane, česar ne moremo.
Nato je težjo stvar izrekla kot vprašanje. Kletka bo pristala na šestih metrih poledenele letve in nekdo bo moral skozi preddverno komoro ter jo z vročo cevjo očistiti pred 10:40.

**Marit Osei**  
Nihče ne bo dobil ukaza. Če ne gre nihče, jo očistimo iz notranjosti kletke, kar pomeni osemnajst minut vkrcavanja. Prvo dvigalo bo zamudilo 12:54 in počakalo do 16:08. Ceno vam povem zato, da lahko rečete ne in veste, kaj to pomeni.

**Anselm Dube**  
Vsi v tej sobi dolgujemo dekompresijski mizi tri dni. Telo, ki je delalo v preddverni komori, ji dolguje še štirideset ur. Nihče naj se ne pretvarja, da to ni nič.

Dva človeka sta jasno rekla ne in Marit je njuni imeni zapisala brez besede. Maud Okonkwo je šla, ker je samo ona poznala letev, Anselm, ker je že delal v preddverni komori, in Kofi Mensah, ker je vprašal, kaj močni dolgujejo bolnim, in mu tišina, ki je sledila, ni bila všeč. Maud se je ob 9:25 vrnila skozi zaporo z ledom v manšetah in prevzela slušalke.

scenes.title: Osem minut
paragraphs: *Ovratnik, 3.350 m spodaj · Ura 9, 40 minut*

Illuminara se je spustila ob kablu, mimo točke, kjer je bila svetloba zgolj ideja, mraz in pritisk pa sta ji pomenila to, kar sta ji pomenila vedno: informacijo. Čutila je, kje led nosi obremenitev in kje se namerava zapreti.
Curlew je visel pri ovratniku z zloženim ogrodjem v trebuhu. Solanov glas v vodi je bil miren in rahlo hripav.

**Imre Solano**  
Oporniki se nameščajo. Stene prehoda so meter narazen. Sulica čez dve minuti. Vršno okno se odpira zdaj.

Oporniki so prevzeli stene. Tako so se dogovorili in olajšanje je bilo biti samo druga polovica. Prevzela je težo kletke. Prišla je vanjo kot zadržan ton, štirinajst ton letve in jekla, ki ju je led skušal obdržati. Prvi voziček je popustil v drugi minuti. Drugi v četrti. Tretji ni.

**Imre Solano**  
Tretji voziček ne popušča. Peta minuta. Še tri.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
Ta voziček ima strižni zatič na vzhodni strani. To je tisti, za katerega sem vedno govorila, da ga moramo zamenjati. Udari ga z vzhoda.

Solano je zasukal sulico. Illuminara je začutila, kako se je zatič v drobnem svetlem zlomu vdal, in kletka se je prvič po 03:40 izmaknila ledu ter sedla na čisto letev in lastne zobnike. Spustila jo je v sedmi minuti in petdeseti sekundi.

**Illuminara**  
Toliko časa zmorem držati. Če bi potrebovala še deset sekund, ji jih ne bi mogla dati jaz.

Kletka se je po dve desetinki metra na sekundo veličastno počasi spuščala proti habitatu in glasovi iz Halcyona so začeli vzklikati, ona pa jim je dovolila. Sama ni šla gor. Okna ne bi čakala, da se vrne dol, zato je ostala v zavetrju ogrodja, v temi.

Ob 11:17, v prvi dolini, so oporniki sami prevzeli led in Solano, ki se je v Curlewu dvigal, je po telemetriji odčital vrednosti: oseminpetdeset odstotkov nazivne vrednosti, enajst milimetrov premika.

**Imre Solano**  
Znotraj meje. Vkrcajte jih.

Ob 11:55 jih je bilo vkrcanih dvanajst, nosila pa so bila pritrjena. Ob 12:50 je kletka prispela do ovratnika in tokrat je bila v njej teža, ki je imela imena. Čez štirinajst metrov jo je držala sedem minut in trideset sekund. Oporniki so držali stene. Curlew je ob 12:55 prebil površje, njegova odprava je bila porabljena, upravljan je bil enkrat, kot obljubljeno.

Kletka se je nato po odprti vrtini vzpenjala še štiri ure in devetintrideset minut, v njej pa je tlak ostal pri šestih barih. Ob 17:40 so se njena vrata spojila z vrati komore na postaji Marrow in prvih dvanajst je začelo prehajati na površinski tlak s hitrostjo, ki so jo dovoljevala njihova telesa.

scenes.title: Druga vožnja
paragraphs: *Ovratnik, 3.350 m spodaj · Ura 22, 40 minut*

Prazna kletka se je po urniku spuščala po vrtini in prav v tem je bila težava. Ustavila se je na poledeneli letvi štiri minute po vrhu ob 22:36, Illuminara pa je čutila, kako se skozi led že vrača stiskanje.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
Štiri minute. Povej naravnost, da lahko nehamo računati. Jo lahko držiš?

**Illuminara**  
Ne čez ves odsek. Imela bi manj kot tri minute, prečkanje pa jih potrebuje sedem. Led bi se sredi letve zaprl okoli kletke. Naslednje okno je ob 25:50.
Nihče po kablu ni predlagal, naj poskusi. Njena gotovost glede lastne omejitve ni še nikoli nikogar stala ničesar; zdaj jih je stala tri ure in štirinajst minut zraka, ki ga je Halcyon lahko preštel.

Ogrodje je skozi dolgo čakanje stalo samo, na lastnih celicah in s podatki po paru v kablu, Maud pa je beležila vsako dolino. Premik 1,4 centimetra ob 14:31. Dve celi nič ob 17:45. Dve celi šest ob 20:59, znotraj meje. Nato ob 24:13, ko je bila kletka parkirana nad njim in se ni nič premikalo, dve celi dve.

Ob 25:50 je Illuminara prazno kletko prenesla čez. Ob 26:52 se je ustavila na pristanku, ki ga je očistila ekipa iz preddverne komore, enajst ljudi pa se je zbralo pri njenih vratih s hitrostjo ljudi, ki lahko hodijo.

**Imre Solano**  
Dolina, 27:27. Sto štiri kilonjutne, premik dve celi šest centimetra. Meja je sto dvajset in tri. Znotraj je in jaz bi vam dovolil prečkati.

**Marit Osei**  
Znotraj meje je odločitev naša. En glas zadostuje. Kdo zavrača?

**Kofi Mensah**  
Jaz. Eno okno. Poglejte zapis: ob 20:59 je kazal dve celi šest, ob 24:13 pa je bil spet pri dve celi dve, ne da bi se ga kdo dotaknil. Raje plačam z zrakom, kot da bi prečkal pri dve celi šest z enajstimi ljudmi v kletki.

**Maud Okonkwo**  
Sled bere pravilno. Res se sprosti.

**Anselm Dube**  
Tri ure štirinajst.

**Marit Osei**  
Prešteto. Imamo devetindvajset ur zraka, prečkanje pa potrebuje pet. Zavrnitev velja. Prečkamo ob 32:18.

Čakali so. Ob 30:41 je dolina pokazala dve celi tri centimetra. Ob 31:15 je kletka zapustila pristanek in ob 32:18 je Illuminara utrujena prevzela njeno težo ter jo prenesla čez v sedmih minutah in petnajstih sekundah, petnajst sekund manj od časa, ki ga je napovedala. Nato se je ob njej dvigala štiri ure in devetintrideset minut s hitrostjo dve desetinki metra na sekundo, kar se ji je zdelo dolgočasno, a se je tega držala.
Ob 37:04 so se vrata spojila. Marit Osei je stopila skoznje zadnja.

**Marit Osei**  
To je vseh enajst. Svoji direktorici lahko poveste, da je habitat izklopljen.

**Ofelia Brandt**  
Podjetje bo želelo vedeti, kdo je kriv za zamrznitev.

**Marit Osei**  
Podjetje lahko to napiše na katero koli tablo želi. Triindvajset ljudi je v komori z vrati.

Maud, Anselm in Kofi so brez pritožb sprejeli dodatnih štirideset ur na dekompresijski mizi. Illuminara je prvič, odkar se je vrnila, sedla na tla nadzorne sobe. Ni se pretvarjala, da ni utrujena. To je jasno povedala sobi in Solanu.
Na steni je nekdo končno izbrisal številke. Namesto njih je bilo s flomastrom zapisano število 23 in pod njim črta.

translation_sl.critic_line: Triindvajset ljudi uide izpod štirih kilometrov ledu, ker Illuminara enkratno plovilo porabi za orodje namesto za šest sedežev, natančno pove, kje se konča njena moč, ujeti posadki pa prepusti dokaze in pristojnost za izbiro zadnjega prečkanja.
